newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes esp sour weaken; LLS diff firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes esp sour weaken; LLS diff firms.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were weaker early Wednesday, particulary West Texas Sour/Midland which continued to see its discount deepen in the face of increased supply.
Against the trend, Light Louisiana Sweet/St James firmed up another couple of cents in anticipation of lower August North Sea Brent supply.
Outright crude futures prices for benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI/Cushing) traded down to a low of $19.38 early and were off 29 cents at $19.44 just after noon.

Driving the market was Tuesday evening's American Petroleum Insitute report showing building crude stocks, a weaker-than-expected draw in gasoline stocks for the July 4 holiday week and continued high products production/refinery runs East of the Rockies, traders and analysts said.
On top of that, sour crudes were hit by news that Iraq's resumed exports moved a step closer as Baghdad handed a draft aid distribution plan to United Nations experts on Tuesday evening.

"The Iraqi situation is hanging over the market to a large extent. Even though exports won't hit the Gulf (of Mexico) until around September, there will be a knee-jerk reaction when a definitive deal is done," said a trader at a medium-sized East Coast integrated oil company.

The strength of WTS through June was partly due to the absence of Iraqi crude but also steady buying by refiners, said a trader for a Texas "mini-major". He says weakness in the last few days is due mainly to extra Canadian sour barrels on the market.
WTS traded at $1.24 and $1.25 under WTI Wednesday, having traded as high as $1.00 under late last week.

LLS has moved in the opposite direction, trading at a $0.25 premium to WTI on Wednesday having moved up from a 25 cent discount in early June. The improvement has been mainly a function of the availability of Brent, traders said.
"Every day it looks less and less likely we'll see Brent cargoes (in July)," said a major oil company crude trader. Also, August's loading program is expected to be lower, he said.

Meanwhile, Eugene Island was down in sympathy with weaker sour, trading at $1.38/$1.40 under WTI on Wednesday. Some traders thought Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire, quoted at 50/55 cents under LLS, was a bit too weak compared with firming LLS.
